answer:
I can't see the bank's reviewed agreements, so this reflects standard US ETF Authorized Participant (AP) agreement and SAI practice. Verify the figures against your review.

- **Collateral required:** An AP allowed to create before delivering all deposit securities must post cash collateral, typically **up to 115%** of the shortfall. Some sponsors specify a range (e.g., at least 105%, up to 115%); a few go higher, around 125%.
- **What the percentage applies to:** The **market value of the undelivered deposit securities**, marked to market daily. If value rises, the AP posts more collateral. If the AP fails to deliver, the fund can use the cash to buy the securities, with the AP covering any shortfall and costs.
- **Is it universal?** No. Rates vary by sponsor, fund and agreement. Each fund's AP agreement and SAI set the actual terms, which the issuer can usually adjust.
